title: AI Token Demand Monitor, as of Sun 8 Nov 2026 (Europe/Zurich)
bottom_line: Token volume still supports the capex trajectory. The constraint has moved to financing cost, permitting and revenue per token: credit, not demand, is the transmission risk this week.

readings.label: Anthropic Q3 compute / revenue
readings.note: Q3 revenue $17.0bn and compute and infrastructure expense $9.9bn (Q2 $5.6bn) from the S-1/A filed 2 Nov, as recorded in the 4 Nov and 8 Nov packs. 9.9/17.0 = 58.2% (d); Q2 was 48% (d). Commitments in that filing were ~$895.4bn; Amendment 2 on 10 Nov raised the aggregate to $900.9bn (see circular-financing feed).

crack_watch.title: Volume up, spend lags
crack_watch.text: Portkey tokens +15.3% vs cost +4.4%; Ramp Tokenomics volume +37.1% vs spend +8.9% (week to 23 Oct vs 25 Sep).

crack_watch.text: No new Ramp adoption month after Sep 2026.

crack_watch.title: Cheap / open-weight share
crack_watch.text: DeepSeek 39.1% of OpenRouter 7-day tokens; frontier trio 18.8%. Contrary: Anthropic 60.5% of Ramp Tokenomics spend.

crack_watch.title: Developer vs enterprise
crack_watch.text: npm mixed (claude-code +10.3%, codex −7.2%, Mon–Sat windows); enterprise adoption data stale.

crack_watch.title: Unit economics
crack_watch.text: Anthropic compute/revenue 58% in Q3 vs 48% in Q2 (d). Contrary: Portkey cost +18.5% since week of 27 Sep, tokens +81.4% (d).

caveats: OpenRouter: no spend in the API since 14 Oct; the week of 2 Nov is partial (Sunday incomplete at the 8 Nov 17:42 Europe/Zurich snapshot) and is not used as a reading. OpenRouter excludes first-party apps. Changes, shares and ratios are derived (d).

Ramp: Tokenomics table unchanged since the 1 Nov vintage (week to 23 Oct vs 25 Sep). Weekly chart series end at the week of 5 Oct (18 Oct vintage). Chart and table are different cuts and are not spliced. Ramp is a US-corporate, API-heavy sample whose composition can change.
Vercel: open/closed traffic split stopped on 17 Oct; team-preference series stuck at 29 Oct (12.65%). The two measures are not comparable and are not spliced.
Portkey: chart-array sums do not match the page headline cards (weekly card spend was −0.0% vs chart +4.4%). Use within-series changes only.
npm includes CI installs; tokensperday.com is stale since 16 Jul 2026 and is not shown.

This edition's bottom line on financing/credit uses only the circular-financing feed and public filings on this page. Broker forecasts and terminal credit prints cited in the original pack are excluded from this public page (see excluded).

Charts in section 3 are Chart.js redraws of the 8 Nov 2026 pack from public OpenRouter, Ramp, Vercel and Portkey series already in this feed. Earlier edition images of the same public series are not shown separately.

bot_charts.intro: Charts from the Token Demand Bot weekly pack of Sunday 8 Nov 2026, 18:32 Europe/Zurich. Redrawn in Chart.js from the same public OpenRouter, Ramp, Vercel and Portkey series already in this feed. Captions, source lines and V / (d) labels follow the pack. The Circular Financing Alert Bot did not produce a public-safe native chart in the saved files; official-flag figures are tabulated in section 2. Screenshots of third-party documents or sites, and charts built on credit-terminal or licensed prints, are not shown.

items.title: OpenRouter: weekly token volume and growth
items.caption: OpenRouter weekly tokens, trailing 12 complete weeks plus the partial week of 2 Nov (202.3T at the 8 Nov 17:42 snapshot; Sunday incomplete, not a final reading). The week of 26 Oct closed at 193.6T (+3.0% WoW after +14.6%, +16.7% over 4 weeks; derived), the highest complete week in the series. Orange = stealth/free models named in the weekly top-9 only; none were in the top-9 in the last two weeks.
